geometry.note: 'verified': representation is 'surveyed' (a published coordinate) from a rank<=10 source. The coordinate is a software constant quoted to six decimals; its own survey is not published, so accuracy_m is set to 10 m.
geometry.quote: The returned location corresponds to the position of the DISC borehole which is used as the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system, i.e., this locations acts as a reference point to define the station positions. ... return (72.582793, -38.455815)

method: Published coordinate used verbatim: the RNO-G detector code returns (72.582793 N, -38.455815 E) as the position of the DISC borehole, 'used as the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system'. The RNO-G station paper's Figure 1 also marks a 'DISC Borehole' beside 'Big House' at that spot (viewed, not traced).
name: DISC borehole, the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system
notes: Drawn so that the station offsets have a visible origin; it is not an RNO-G instrument.

summary.plain: The Deep Ice Sheet Coring (DISC) borehole near Summit Station, the reference point from which the RNO-G station positions are measured.
